# <span class="en">Implications for transport planning</span><span class="zh">对交通规划的启示</span> {#sec-implications}

::: {.en}
The handout's list of report sections carries over wording from the previous exercise ("peace-keeping", "public safety"). This section
reads those as implications for the policy question this exercise poses, which is sustainable rail planning. These are one student's readings of a model with the limits set out in
@sec-limits, offered as questions the analysis raises rather than as recommendations to a transport authority.

**Sequence shell stations by land use, not by line.** The stations at risk of low ridership are identifiable well ahead of time: Aviation Park, Jurong Pier,
Tengah, Jurong Hill. The Hume and Woodleigh precedent suggests a choice that an operator can revisit: build the structure with the line, and tie fit-out and opening to a
measurable threshold in the surrounding market. Keppel, open and nearly empty, shows the running cost of doing the opposite.

**Plan interchanges for transfers, not for the tap-ins this report predicts.** Boon Lay, Hougang, Ang Mo Kio and Choa Chu Kang each stand to gain tens of thousands of daily
transfers. Station-level ridership would not reveal this, and a forecast of falling tap-ins at Boon Lay could read as reassurance. Boon Lay in particular has no
transfer flow today.

**Expect western East-West stations to change character.** Pioneer, Lakeside and Chinese Garden lose much of their home-end catchment, as
do feeder bus routes that serve them today. Bus network planning is the natural counterpart. The riders who leave these stations are those who lived furthest from them, so
the same residents with shorter access is a gain, even though the station's tap-ins fall.

**Measure the opening.** The largest unknown in this report, how much ridership a new line creates, could be settled by data the system already
produces. Stage-by-stage openings of the Jurong Region Line from 2028 are a natural experiment. Saving OD data around each one, which DataMall deletes after three
months, would allow a before-and-after estimate that no cross-section can give.
:::

::: {.zh}
手册所列的报告章节沿用了上一次作业的措辞（“维和”“公共安全”）。本节把它们理解为本次作业所提政策问题的启示，即可持续的轨道规划。这些只是一名学生基于具有 @sec-limits 所述局限的模型所作的解读，是分析提出的问题，而非对交通主管部门的建议。

**按土地利用而非线路安排外壳车站的时序。** 低客流风险的车站可以提前识别：Aviation Park、Jurong Pier、Tengah、Jurong Hill。Hume 与 Woodleigh 的先例提示了一个可以调整的选择：随线路建好结构，并把装修与开放与周边市场的可测阈值挂钩。Keppel 已开放却几乎无人使用，显示了相反做法的运营代价。

**按换乘而不是本报告预测的进站量来规划换乘站。** Boon Lay、Hougang、Ang Mo Kio 与 Choa Chu Kang 每日都将增加数万次换乘。车站层面的客流不会显示这一点，而 Boon Lay 进站量下降的预测甚至可能被解读为令人安心。Boon Lay 今天尤其没有换乘客流。

**预期东西线西段车站的性质改变。** Pioneer、Lakeside 与 Chinese Garden 将失去大部分居住端集散范围，服务它们的接驳公交也是如此。公交网络规划是自然的配套。离开这些车站的乘客是住得最远的那些人，所以同样的居民到达距离变短是一种收益，尽管车站的进站量下降。

**对开通进行测量。** 本报告最大的未知数，也就是新线能创造多少客流，可以用系统已经产生的数据来回答。裕廊区域线自 2028 年起的分阶段开通是天然实验。保存每次开通前后的 OD 数据（DataMall 三个月后即删除），就能得到任何截面数据都无法提供的前后对比估计。
:::
